entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Be careful if you do go. A number of[n]strange incidents and accidents have[n]been occurring lately.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Ah, yes, I had almost forgotten. There hasn't[n]been much talk about it lately.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: My hostess was talking about a group[n]called the Phantom Thieves. Have you[n]heard about them?

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Yes, they're the ones with the "calling[n]card." I heard they had an altercation[n]with the yakuza.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: They seem to be very popular among[n]young people. Though I don't know why.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: There's no telling why these days.[n]However, I believe they may be able[n]to build their own business.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Junya Kaneshiro quite incredibly[n]invaded both the financial markets[n]and the political world.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: A lot of business executives appear to be[n]nervous about his arrest.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I didn't know he was such a big deal...[n]Bravo to the Phantom Thieves.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: We shouldn't celebrate them just yet...[n]They still remain suspicious.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Medjed's statement is essentially a[n]declaration of terrorism. Is the[n]government going to do anything?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: They have likely given up. No one has[n]been able to discover their true identities.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Which means we must rely on the[n]Phantom Thieves. Though, I doubt[n]they'll be amenable.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Regardless, they're garnering a lot of[n]attention... So, shall we put an ad on[n]the news station?

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I'm surprised to see you, Executive[n]Director. I thought you were on[n]vacation in Europe...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: The company ordered me to return. I'm[n]sure you're aware of the actions Medjed[n]is taking.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: The hacking incident, yes? Are we being[n]targeted now?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: We must prepare for the worst. The initial[n]response is crucial in these types of[n]situations.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Well, the whole thing with Medjed turned[n]out to be anticlimactic, didn't it?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: We should be relieved that nothing[n]happened. What's more ominous is[n]the Phantom Thieves.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: How so? I thought they did well this time...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Gaining power moves one closer to[n]becoming an authoritarian. That's just[n]the way of the world.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: As expected... The greater public has sided[n]with the Phantom Thieves.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Yes, even though many were skeptical of[n]them until recently.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: We hate to think, therefore we are easily[n]controlled. Japan is becoming a country[n]of imbeciles.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I guess that means there's going to be[n]people making a fortune off of them again.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I pity Okumura, however that could easily[n]be us tomorrow.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Our company isn't like that. We're very[n]much on the level.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I am not so sure about that... The internet[n]and media are both skilled at starting fires.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: In that respect, I sort of envy him. To think[n]that could happen to us when we're all[n]working so hard.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I heard that President Okumura passed[n]away.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I wonder if the Okumura empire is over[n]now without him at the helm.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Many people sympathize with him. Their[n]stock price hit rock-bottom, but it has[n]since rebounded.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: So then he was a sacrificial lamb for their[n]business... What a world we live in.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: The media know no shame. First they[n]incite all that Phantom Thieves[n]pandemonium, and now this.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Those who are swayed by fads are fools.[n]The people of this country will never learn.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Is this really what we should be focusing[n]on? Aren't the elections at the end of[n]the year?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Yes, and the ruling party finally split up.[n]Although, it's too late, considering the[n]approval rating.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Currently, there's the ruling party, the[n]opposition, and that new party. An[n]exciting three-way fight.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: ...You think so? I believe the final outcome[n]is a foregone conclusion.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: The new political party will definitely win.[n]Their leader is a master of media.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I see... Although it IS a national election,[n]which is basically a popular vote...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: At a special board meeting, we decided[n]that our group is going to back Shido.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: So we're making our donations to the[n]new political party, then? Not surprising,[n]I suppose.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: It's a strategic move so that we don't miss[n]the boat. We want to be connected to the[n]new government.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: How's the election going? The number[n]of Shido supporters doesn't appear to[n]be decreasing.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: A huge movement won't change much.[n]The company has decided to take a[n]wait-and-see approach.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: It might be different if we had a back-up[n]plan but I haven't seen any movement[n]since that notice.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: Out of the frying pan and into the fire,[n]as they say, hm? Who does this country[n]belong to...?

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I never thought about that... What's going[n]on all of a sudden?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I am not sure of anything any more. Not[n]even what I'll be doing this time next year...

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: D-Director, please don't talk like that.[n]You're scaring me.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Director, is it true that you don't like[n]worshipping at shrines?

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I've never understood why people turn to[n]god to grant their wishes.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: A wish is something you must fulfill with[n]your own power. You shouldn't rely on[n]someone else to do it for you.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I see... Considering that you survived this[n]industry all on your own, I can see why[n]you would think that way.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: What do you think about the current[n]economy? Business seems to be booming[n]for everyone...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I feel unsettled by it.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: That... wasn't the kind of response I was[n]expecting. Everyone seems to be in high[n]spirits though...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: When all people conform and feel the[n]same emotion... That's when things[n]are most dangerous.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: No one seems to be talking about the[n]Phantom Thieves anymore.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: I've read online that someone made[n]them up as a prank. They've even[n]uploaded proof.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: And yet, I still believe that the Phantom[n]Thieves are real. Is that silly?

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: Not at all... I believe in them more than[n]I do Shido. Maybe the Phantom Thieves[n]stole our hearts too...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: There are many lessons we can learn from[n]this past year. This country hasn't matured.

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: It is so fragile, both inside and out. It could[n]crumble from the slightest tremor.

entries.speaker: Earnest Office Worker
entries.en: You're right... but there are some who[n]display a fighting spirit, like the Phantom[n]Thieves...

entries.speaker: Elderly Office Worker
entries.en: I hope the lessons of this year remain[n]within the hearts of the young for the[n]rest of their lives.
